360: Rotation, Spotting and Landing Orientation

  • Outline: needs authoring
  • Class 3
  • Release C

For the reviewer

Text-verified source
Yes

The reviewer must supply or confirm:

  • Technique: coach-authored movement phases, cues and timing for this trick.
  • Progression: coach-authored stages with consistency gates, feature selection and facility requirements.
  • Corrections: a coach-approved correction for each common error.
  • Readiness: the prerequisites and stop criteria the coach will check in person.

Watch or read before signing off (not yet checked):

  • t03: How to 360 with Ray George (Video only: not yet watched)
  • t11: How to do a 360 degree turn on a Mountain Bike? (Video only: not yet watched)
  • t02: Slopestyle: Advanced Drops and Jumps (Outline only)

Lesson goal

Understand the 360’s components at a conceptual level and the questions a coach uses to diagnose it.

What it will cover

  • Compare Ray George, Tom Cardy and MTB Hopper perspectives
  • Concepts: feature choice, takeoff, rotation, visual orientation, landing alignment
  • 360 off a jump versus off a drop
  • Diagnostic questions: under- and over-rotation, off-axis takeoff, losing the spot

Physics & maths

Angular momentum: once in the air, a rider’s rotation can only be adjusted by changing body shape, not started from nothing.

Safety

Class 3: high-consequence skills. Theory and expert references only. Any practical progression is authored and supervised in person by a verified specialist coach, in a suitable facility.

Practice only on terrain your coach has chosen, within your current skill, with the right protective equipment. Completing a lesson isn’t a safety certificate and doesn’t mean a rider is ready to try anything.
